title: Abide with Me
by: Henry Francis Lyte · tune Eventide by William Henry Monk
note: Written by a dying vicar in Devon weeks before his death, as evening fell over the sea. It has been sung before the FA Cup Final since 1927, and gives this app its name.

title: The Lord's My Shepherd (Crimond)
by: Psalm 23 from the Scottish Psalter (1650) · tune Crimond (1872)
note: Scotland's best-loved psalm, sung at weddings and funerals across the country, and at Queen Elizabeth II's wedding in 1947. The plainest words set to the gentlest tune.

title: Be Thou My Vision
by: Old Irish, translated by Mary Byrne (1905) and Eleanor Hull (1912) · tune Slane
note: A prayer from early Irish monasticism, set to a folk melody. A morning prayer in itself: asking that God be the first thing we see.

title: Amazing Grace
note: Written by a former slave-ship captain who became a clergyman and an ally of the abolitionists. A hymn about being found by grace when you least deserved it.

title: Holy, Holy, Holy
by: Reginald Heber · tune Nicaea by John Bacchus Dykes
note: A hymn to the Trinity, drawn from the worship of heaven in Revelation 4. Majestic, and easy to sing.

title: Dear Lord and Father of Mankind
by: John Greenleaf Whittier · tune Repton by Hubert Parry
note: Written by a Quaker poet, it asks for the "still small voice of calm". A perfect hymn for a pause in a busy day.
search: Dear Lord and Father of Mankind

title: It Is Well with My Soul
by: Horatio Spafford · tune by Philip Bliss
note: Spafford wrote it after his four daughters drowned in a shipwreck, as his own ship passed the place where they died. Faith that holds in the worst of grief.
search: It Is Well with My Soul

title: In Christ Alone
note: A modern hymn from Northern Ireland that tells the whole Christian story in four verses. Now sung around the world.

title: O Sacred Head, Now Wounded
by: Medieval Latin, German by Paul Gerhardt (1656) · melody by Hans Leo Hassler
note: A meditation on the crucified Christ. Bach loved its melody so much that he set it five times in the St Matthew Passion.

title: Miserere mei, Deus
note: A setting of Psalm 51 for the Sistine Chapel, where it was kept so secret that, by the famous story, the 14-year-old Mozart wrote it down from memory after one hearing. Listen for the soprano's high C floating above the choir.

title: Spem in alium
note: A motet for forty independent voices, by the great English composer of the Reformation era. Like standing inside a cathedral made of sound.

title: St Matthew Passion
note: The story of Christ's suffering and death, for two choirs and two orchestras. Often called the greatest work of Western music. Start with the opening chorus and the aria "Erbarme dich".
search: St Matthew Passion Johann Sebastian Bach

title: Mass in B minor
note: Bach's summing-up of a lifetime, written by a Lutheran setting the Latin Mass. He signed his scores "Soli Deo Gloria": to God alone the glory.
search: Mass in B minor Johann Sebastian Bach

title: Messiah
note: Composed in about three weeks and first performed in Dublin in 1742 for charity. Audiences still stand for the Hallelujah Chorus.

title: Ave verum corpus
note: Just 46 bars, written months before Mozart's death. Three minutes of perfect stillness.
search: Ave verum corpus Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart

title: Requiem
note: A Requiem without terror: Fauré left out most of the Day of Judgement and ended with "In Paradisum", the angels leading the soul into paradise. Music for grief that consoles.

title: All-Night Vigil
note: Russian Orthodox evening and morning prayer for unaccompanied choir, written as the old world collapsed into war. Listen for the very low basses at the end of the fifth movement.

title: O virtus Sapientiae
note: Chant by a German abbess, visionary, scientist and composer, one of the first composers whose name we know. A single line of melody that soars.
search: O virtus Sapientiae Hildegard of Bingen

title: Salve Regina
note: Monks have sung this at the end of Compline for centuries, the last sound of the monastery day before the great silence.

title: Spiegel im Spiegel
note: By an Estonian Orthodox composer who fell silent for years and returned with a new, simple style he called "tintinnabuli", like bells. Music that slows your breathing.

title: Song for Athene
note: Written in memory of a family friend, and sung as Princess Diana's coffin left Westminster Abbey in 1997. Words from the Orthodox funeral service over a single held note.

title: Miserere
note: Psalm 51 again, by Scotland's leading living composer, a Catholic from Ayrshire. Ancient and modern at once.

title: Symphony No. 3 (Symphony of Sorrowful Songs)
note: The second movement sets a prayer to Mary that an 18-year-old girl wrote on the wall of a Gestapo cell. A 1992 recording sold over a million copies.
search: Symphony No. 3 (Symphony of Sorrowful Songs) Henryk Górecki

title: Amazing Grace (live album)
note: Recorded live in a Los Angeles Baptist church, returning to the gospel music she grew up with. One of the best-selling gospel albums of all time.

title: Precious Lord, Take My Hand
by: Thomas A. Dorsey · sung by Mahalia Jackson
note: Written by the father of gospel music after his wife and newborn son died. Martin Luther King Jr.'s favourite song; Mahalia Jackson sang it at his funeral.
search: Precious Lord, Take My Hand Thomas A. Dorsey

title: How Great Thou Art
note: Elvis's own favourite kind of music was gospel. This album won him a Grammy; the hymn itself began as a Swedish poem in 1885.
search: How Great Thou Art Elvis Presley

note: A setting of Psalm 40 that U2 used to close their concerts for years, with tens of thousands singing "How long to sing this song?"

title: Every Grain of Sand
note: From Dylan's Christian years: a quiet confession about seeing God's hand in the smallest things.
search: Every Grain of Sand Bob Dylan

title: The Man Comes Around
note: Written near the end of his life from the imagery of the Book of Revelation. A man in black facing judgement and mercy.
search: The Man Comes Around Johnny Cash

title: Seven Swans
note: An album of quiet songs about faith, doubt and Bible stories, for banjo and voice.

title: Hallelujah
note: Not a worship song, and not by a Christian, but full of King David and the longing for God. Included because it is how many people first say the word "hallelujah".

title: Morning Has Broken
by: Eleanor Farjeon (1931) · sung by Cat Stevens
note: A hymn about creation made new each day, set to a Scottish Gaelic melody, which became a 1971 hit.

title: O Come, O Come, Emmanuel
by: Medieval Advent antiphons, translated by John Mason Neale (1851)
note: Built from the ancient 'O Antiphons', sung in the last days before Christmas. Its minor-key longing is the sound of Advent: waiting in the dark for God to come.

title: O Radiant Dawn
note: The Scottish composer's setting of the Advent prayer to Christ as the dawn, from his Strathclyde Motets. Four minutes of light breaking through.

title: In the Bleak Midwinter
by: Christina Rossetti · music by Gustav Holst or Harold Darke
note: Rossetti's poem asks what we can give the Christ child, and answers: give him my heart. Darke's setting was voted the greatest carol by choral experts in 2008.

title: O Come, All Ye Faithful (Adeste Fideles)
note: The great Christmas procession hymn. Listen for the descant soaring over the last verse in a cathedral recording.
search: O Come, All Ye Faithful (Adeste Fideles)

title: Silent Night
note: First sung with a guitar in a village church in Austria on Christmas Eve 1818. Soldiers sang it across the trenches in the Christmas truce of 1914.

title: Good King Wenceslas
note: A carol about a 10th-century duke who went out on St Stephen's Day to help a poor man: Christmas faith turned into action.

title: We Three Kings
note: An Epiphany carol in which each wise man explains his gift: gold for a king, incense for God, myrrh for one who will die.

title: Christ the Lord Is Risen Today
note: The Easter hymn, with its rolling 'Alleluias'. Written by the brother of John Wesley, founders of Methodism.
search: Christ the Lord Is Risen Today

title: Come Down, O Love Divine
by: Bianco da Siena, translated by Richard Littledale · tune Down Ampney by Ralph Vaughan Williams
note: A medieval Italian prayer to the Holy Spirit, set to a tune Vaughan Williams named after the village where he was born. A Pentecost favourite.

title: Veni Creator Spiritus
note: "Come, Creator Spirit": sung at Pentecost, at ordinations and at coronations for over a thousand years.

title: All Creatures of Our God and King
by: St Francis of Assisi, paraphrased by William Draper
note: Based on Francis's Canticle of the Sun, in which he calls the sun his brother and the moon his sister. A hymn of the whole creation praising God.
search: All Creatures of Our God and King

title: For All the Saints
by: William Walsham How · tune Sine Nomine by Ralph Vaughan Williams
note: The hymn of All Saints' Day, a great march of the faithful through history. Vaughan Williams's tune is one of the finest of the 20th century.

title: Were You There (When They Crucified My Lord)
note: A spiritual that places you at the foot of the cross. Its quiet question has made people weep for over a century.
search: Were You There (When They Crucified My Lord)

title: Ubi caritas
by: Ancient chant · setting by Maurice Duruflé
note: "Where charity and love are, God is there." Sung on Maundy Thursday at the washing of feet. Duruflé's version keeps the old chant at its heart.

title: All Glory, Laud and Honour
by: Theodulf of Orléans, translated by John Mason Neale
note: The Palm Sunday hymn, written by a bishop in prison, it is said, and sung as processions enter church waving palms.

title: Great Is Thy Faithfulness
note: Based on Lamentations 3: faith found not in a crisis but in ordinary days, "morning by morning".

title: Jesu, Joy of Man's Desiring
note: A chorale that flows like water over a gentle triplet melody, from a cantata Bach wrote in his first year in Leipzig. Perhaps the most loved three minutes he wrote.
search: Jesu, Joy of Man's Desiring Johann Sebastian Bach

title: Wachet auf, ruft uns die Stimme
note: "Sleepers, wake!" Based on Jesus' parable of the bridesmaids waiting with their lamps. Listen for the tenors singing the chorale over the strings' dancing melody.
search: Wachet auf, ruft uns die Stimme Johann Sebastian Bach

title: Christmas Oratorio
note: Six cantatas for the twelve days of Christmas, opening with drums and trumpets: "Jauchzet, frohlocket!" (Shout for joy!)

title: Magnificat
note: Mary's song of praise, "My soul magnifies the Lord", sung at Evening Prayer for centuries. Bach makes it blaze with trumpets.

title: Komm, süßer Tod
note: "Come, sweet death": a short sacred song about longing for rest in God, often heard in quiet orchestral arrangements.
search: Komm, süßer Tod Johann Sebastian Bach

title: Gloria
note: Written by the "red priest" of Venice for the girls' choir of the orphanage where he taught. Bright, joyful and full of energy.

title: Vespers of the Blessed Virgin
note: A vast, glittering setting of Evening Prayer that bridges Renaissance and Baroque music. Built for the echoing space of an Italian church.
search: Vespers of the Blessed Virgin Claudio Monteverdi

title: Missa Papae Marcelli
note: Legend says this Mass, with words clear above the weaving voices, persuaded the Church not to ban complex polyphony. Pure, balanced and serene.
search: Missa Papae Marcelli Giovanni Pierluigi da Palestrina

title: Mass for Four Voices
note: Written by a Catholic in Elizabethan England, for secret Masses in country houses. Intimate music with real courage behind it.
search: Mass for Four Voices William Byrd

title: Zadok the Priest
note: Sung at every British coronation since 1727. The long, rising introduction before the choir bursts in is one of the great moments in music.
search: Zadok the Priest George Frideric Handel

title: The Creation
note: The story of Genesis 1 in music. Listen for the moment at "and there was light", when the whole orchestra and choir explode into a blaze of C major.

title: Elijah
note: The story of the prophet Elijah, first performed in Birmingham. "O rest in the Lord" is one of its best-loved moments.

title: Missa Solemnis
note: Beethoven wrote on the score: "From the heart; may it go to the heart." A huge, searching Mass by a composer who was by then almost completely deaf.

title: A German Requiem
note: Not a prayer for the dead but comfort for the living, with words Brahms chose from Luther's Bible: "Blessed are they that mourn, for they shall be comforted."

title: Locus iste
note: "This place was made by God." A short motet written for the consecration of a chapel in Linz Cathedral. Cathedral music in miniature.

title: The Dream of Gerontius
note: A setting of John Henry Newman's poem about a soul's journey through death to God. Elgar wrote on the score: "This is the best of me."
search: The Dream of Gerontius Edward Elgar

title: Quartet for the End of Time
note: Composed and first performed in a prisoner-of-war camp, for the only instruments available, and inspired by the angel of Revelation 10. Music suspended out of time.
search: Quartet for the End of Time Olivier Messiaen

title: Fantasia on a Theme by Thomas Tallis
note: First performed in Gloucester Cathedral, written to sound like the building itself: a hymn tune by Tallis expanding into vast, echoing space.
search: Fantasia on a Theme by Thomas Tallis Ralph Vaughan Williams

title: Requiem
note: Woven from ancient Gregorian chant, gentle and luminous, by a French cathedral organist.

title: Requiem
note: Left unfinished at Mozart's death and completed by his pupil. The "Lacrimosa" is music on the edge of tears.

title: O magnum mysterium
note: A modern Christmas motet about the animals at the manger. Rich, slow harmonies that feel like candlelight.
